groups.title: Suits in a pack of cards
groups.explanation: A standard pack is divided into these four suits.

groups.title: Garden tools
groups.explanation: Each of these is a tool for turning, weeding or tidying a garden.

groups.title: Card games
groups.explanation: All four are card games for a table of two to six players.

sources.excerpt: While English-speaking countries traditionally use cards with the French suits of clubs, spades, hearts and diamonds, many other countries have their own traditional suits.
Examples include the hatchet, axe, sickle, scythe, pitchfork, spade, shovel, trowel, hoe, fork, and rake.
Whist is a classic English trick-taking card game that was widely played in the 18th and 19th centuries.
Rummy is a group of  games related by the feature of matching cards of the same rank or sequence and same suit.
Canasta (; Spanish for "basket") is a card game of the rummy family of games believed to be a variant of 500 rum.
Cribbage, or crib, is a card game, traditionally for two players, that involves playing and grouping cards in combinations which gain points.

editorNotes: Spade is the tile with two uses, a suit and a digging tool, and the tool group is full once trowel, rake, hoe and fork are together, so spade counts as a suit. Club and diamond have other meanings, but neither is a garden tool, and whist and cribbage are played with cards rather than in a border.
